[[File:1920 Locust yearbook p. 095 (Freshman).jpg|thumb|150px|Freshman class artwork, from [[East Texas State Normal College]]'s 1920 ''Locust'' yearbook]]
A '''freshman''', '''fresher''', '''first year''', or [[colloquially]] '''frosh''',<ref>{{cite web|title=Frosh Definition & Meaning |website=[[Merriam-Webster]] |url=https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/frosh|access-date=August 30, 2023}}</ref> is a person in the first year at an educational institution, usually a [[secondary school]] or at the [[college]] and [[university]] level, but also in other forms of [[post-secondary school|post-secondary educational institutions]] or [[primary school]].

==Arab world==
In much of the [[Arab world]], a first-year is called a {{lang|ar-Latn|mubtadi'}} ({{lang|ar|مبتدئ}}; plural {{lang|ar|مبتدئون}}, {{lang|ar-Latn| mubtadi'ūn}}), which is Arabic for "beginner".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://alghad.com/Section-208/uncategorized/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A7%D9%81%D8%B1-%D9%8A%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%AC%D9%87%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%82%D9%81-%D9%85%D8%B6%D8%AD%D9%83%D8%A9-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A3%D9%88%D9%84-%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A9-%D8%AC%D8%A7%D9%85%D8%B9%D8%A9-397068 |script-title=ar:يواجهون-مواقف-مضحكة-في-أول-سنة-جامعة |lang=ar |trans-title=They face funny situations in the first year of university |date=October 6, 2013 |last=Abu Sobh |first=Mona |newspaper=[[Al Ghad]] |location=[[Jordan]]}}</ref>

==Asia==
Some Asian countries use the same names as used in the United States (freshman, [[sophomore]], [[Junior (education year)|junior]], [[Senior (education year)|senior]]), among them [[Malaysia]].{{Citation needed|reason=proof?|date=April 2026}}

==Brazil==
In [[Brazil]], students that pass the [[vestibular exam]] and begin studying in a college or university are called "''calouros''" or more informally "''bixos''" ("''bixetes''" for girls), an alternate spelling of "''bicho''", which means "animal" (although commonly used to refer to bugs). ''Calouros'' are often subject to [[hazing]], which is known as "''trote''" (lit. "prank") there. The first known hazing episode in Brazil happened in 1831 at the Law School of [[Olinda]] and resulted in the death of a student.<ref name="ME">{{cite web |last1=Nadai |first1=Mariana |title=Quais foram os trotes mais cruéis do Brasil? |url=http://mundoestranho.abril.com.br/materia/os-trotes-maiscrueis-do-brasil |website=[[Mundo Estranho]] |publisher=[[Grupo Abril]] |access-date=2015-02-17 |language=pt|archive-date=2015-02-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150218010546/http://mundoestranho.abril.com.br/materia/os-trotes-maiscrueis-do-brasil |url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1999, a [[Chinese Brazilian]] ''calouro'' of the [[University of São Paulo]] Medicine School named {{ill|Edison Tsung Chi Hsueh|pt|Morte de Edison Tsung Chi Hsueh}} was found dead at the institution's swimming pool; this has since become one of the most well known episodes of violent hazing and has received extensive national media coverage since that year.<ref name="ME" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Toledo |first1=Roberto Pompeu de |title=Tolerância zero, o remédio para o trote |url=http://veja.abril.com.br/210499/p_154.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090218163953/http://veja.abril.com.br/210499/p_154.html |archive-date=2009-02-18 |website=[[Veja (magazine)|Veja]] |publisher=[[Grupo Abril]]|access-date=2015-02-17 |language=pt |date=1999-04-30 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Calouro morre afogado em trote na USP |url=http://www.terra.com.br/noticias/infograficos/30-crimes-que-abalaram-o-brasil/30-crimes05.htm |website=[[Terra Networks|Terra]] |access-date=17 February 2015 |language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Oliveira |first1=Mariana |title=STF mantém absolvição de 4 pela morte de calouro da USP em 1999 |url=http://g1.globo.com/sao-paulo/noticia/2013/06/stf-mantem-absolvicao-de-4-pela-morte-de-calouro-da-usp-em-1999.html |website=G1 |publisher=[[Grupo Globo]] |access-date=17 February 2015 |location=[[Brasília]] |language=pt |date=6 June 2013}}</ref>

==Canada==
The term "first year" is used for a first-year student at university or college. The [[Frosh-week|student orientation period]] at Canadian universities is often called "Frosh week."

== Chile ==
{{lang|es|Mechón}} or {{lang|es|mechona}} is used for the first-year students of [[University of Chile]], a term that has spread to the rest of the universities in the country.

== Croatia ==
The term {{lang|hr|brucoš}} is used for either first-year college or university students or students who haven't yet passed any exams.

==Germany==
In [[Germany]], a first-semester student of a university program (Bachelor, Master, State exam etc) is called {{lang|de|Erstsemester}}, or in short and more common, {{lang|de|Ersti}}, with {{lang|de|erst}} meaning 'first' and the {{lang|de|-i}} adding a benevolently diminutive tone. The plural is {{lang|de|Erstis}}.

Unlike the word ''freshman'', which stands for a student in their whole first ''year'', the German word {{lang|de|Ersti}} is exclusively used for students in their first ''semester''. Students of higher semesters are accordingly called {{lang|de|Zweitsemester}}, {{lang|de|Drittsemester}}, {{lang|de|Viertsemester}} etc. and sometimes, but rarely, also {{lang|de|Zweitis}}, {{lang|de|Drittis}}, {{lang|de|Viertis}}, etc.

==United Kingdom==

===England and Wales===
Students at the beginning of their first year of university are often known in [[England]] and [[Wales]] as ''freshers''; however, the terms ''freshman'' and '<nowiki/>''first years''<nowiki/>' is also used. The first week of term before lessons is widely known as ''freshers' week'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Becoming a Fresher at UoB |publisher=Unihousing |url=https://unihousing.co/news/article/becoming-a-fresher-at-uob |access-date=2023-09-13}}</ref> when there are usually no classes, and students take part in induction events and fairs; but this arrangement is not universal. As freshers are newcomers to the institutions and often experience a period of adjustment as they navigate university life, there are numerous UK websites available that offer support and resources to help freshers with university preparations, such as providing guidance on accommodation, academic advice, social activities, and general tips for a successful start to their university journey.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Freshers|url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/freshers|access-date=21 June 2020|work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Reidy |first=Tess |date=12 November 2019 |title=How to make your first year at uni count – even if your grades don't |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2019/nov/12/make-your-first-year-at-university-count |access-date=2020-06-21|issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Freshers' Week clichés (and how not to be one) |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/articles/znx6jhv |access-date=21 June 2020|website=BBC Bitesize}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Making the most of freshers' week |url=https://www.prospects.ac.uk/applying-for-university/university-life/making-the-most-of-freshers-week |access-date= |first=Jemma |last=Smith |date=September 2021 |website=prospects.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=22 things graduates wish they had known as freshers|url=https://www.savethestudent.org/extra-guides/freshers/23-things-grads-wished-theyd-known-in-their-first-year.html |access-date=21 June 2020|website=Save the Student}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Your Freshers Guide - Freshers Week 2023 |url=https://www.yourfreshersguide.com/ |access-date=2023-07-04 |website=Your Freshers Guide |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Goodger |first=Lottie |title=The best student letting agencies in Birmingham in 2023: Revealed! |url=https://unifresher.co.uk/accommodation/the-best-student-letting-agents-in-birmingham-2/ |access-date=2023-07-04 |website=Unifresher |language=en-US}}</ref>

Unlike in [[Scotland]], this term is not used in reference to pre-university education, the equivalent terms being ''year sevens'' for the first year of [[Secondary education in the United Kingdom|secondary school]] and ''first years'', ''lower sixths'' and ''year twelves'' used at [[Sixth form college|sixth forms]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ferguson |first=Donna |date=2019-08-27 |title='No one will try to terrify you': year 8 advice to year 7s |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2019/aug/27/secondary-school-year-8-advice-to-year-7-no-one-will-try-to-terrify-you |access-date=2020-06-21 |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-09-03 |title=The best (and worst) tips for year sevens starting secondary school |url=http://www.independent.co.uk/voices/iv-drip/the-best-and-worst-tips-for-year-sevens-starting-secondary-school-8796627.html |access-date=2020-06-21 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-05-11 |title=First year sixth form students could return to college on 1 June |url=https://feweek.co.uk/2020/05/11/dfe-announces-first-year-sixth-form-students-could-be-returning-to-college-as-soon-as-1-june/ |access-date=2020-06-21 |website=FE Week}}</ref>

===Scotland===
'''First year''' (also known as '''S1''' in Scotland) is the first year of schooling in [[Secondary education in Scotland|secondary schools in Scotland]] and is roughly equivalent to [[Year Eight (School)|Year 8]] (Second Form) in England and Wales and Year 9 (Second Form) in Northern Ireland. Most pupils are 12 or 13 years old at the end of S1.

{{S-start}}
{{Succession box|before=[[Year 7#Northern Ireland and Scotland|Primary 7]]|title=First year|years=11.5&ndash;13|after=[[Second year]]|}}
{{S-end}}

The first year of primary education in [[Scotland]] is known as '''Primary 1''' ('''P1''').

At the [[Universities in Scotland#Middle Ages|four ancient Scottish universities]] the traditional names for the four years at university are [[Bejan]] ("Bejant" at the [[University of St Andrews]]) (1st),<ref>{{Cite EB1911 |wstitle=Bejan |volume=3 |page=659}}</ref> Semi (2nd), Tertian (3rd) and Magistrand (4th), though all Scottish universities will have a "freshers' week" (as with all British universities) and the term is as widely used with more traditional terms.<ref>{{cite book |last=Grant |first=Sir Alexander |author-link=Sir Alexander Grant, 10th Baronet |title=The story of the University of Edinburgh during its first three hundred years (Vol. 2) |date=1884 |location=London |publisher=Longmans, Green, and co. |page=[https://archive.org/details/b2900312x_0002/page/479 479] |url=https://archive.org/details/b2900312x_0002 |access-date=2 March 2019}}</ref>

==United States==

===Beginner===

Freshman is commonly in use as a [[US English]] [[idiom]]atic term to describe a beginner or novice, someone who is naïve, a first effort, instance, or a student in the first year of study (generally used in both [[high school]] and in [[tertiary school]] university study before the taking of a degree).<ref name="dict-fresh">{{cite web |author=Random House, Inc. |year=2006 |title=freshman |url=http://dictionary.reference.com/browse/freshman |work=Dictionary.com |access-date=12 August 2007}}</ref>

===<span class="anchor" id="First Year Congressional representatives"></span> First year congressional representatives===
<!-- Anchor of "First Year Congressional representatives" is the old name of the section -->
New members of [[United States Congress|Congress]] in their first term are referred to as ''freshmen senators'' or ''freshmen congressmen or congresswomen'', no matter how experienced they were in previous government positions.

===First-year high school students===

High school first-year students are almost exclusively referred to as freshmen, or in some cases by their grade year, [[9th grade]]rs. Second-year students are sophomores, or [[10th grade]]rs, then juniors or [[11th grade]]rs, and finally seniors or [[12th grade]]rs.<ref>{{cite web | title=Here's the Real Reason We Call Students Freshmen, Sophomores, Juniors and Seniors | url=https://www.rd.com/article/freshman-sophomore-junior-senior/ }}</ref>

===First-year university students===

At college or university, freshman denotes students in their first year of study. The grade designations of high school are not used, but the terms [[sophomore]], junior, and senior are kept at most schools. Some colleges, including historically women's colleges, do not use the term freshman but use first year, instead.<ref name="Huffpost College">{{cite web |author=Huffpost College |year=2012 |title=UNC Drops 'Freshman' From School Vocabulary In Favor Of 'First-Year,' Media Controversy Ensues |website=[[HuffPost]] |url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/10/25/unc-freshman-first-year-sexist_n_2016645.html |access-date=15 June 2016}}</ref><ref name="NCF">{{cite web |author=Student Admissions Representatives |year=2010 |title=Meet Our Student Representatives |url=http://www.ncf.edu/student-admission-representatives |publisher=New College of Florida |access-date=19 December 2010 |archive-date=6 February 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110206120618/http://ncf.edu/student-admission-representatives |url-status=dead}}</ref> Beyond the fourth year, students are simply classified as fifth year, sixth year, super senior, etc. Some institutions use the term freshman for specific reporting purposes.<ref name="wisc">{{cite web |author=Office of the Registrar |year=2006 |title=Glossary of Reporting Terms |url=http://registrar.wisc.edu/students/acadrecords/enrollment_reports/85_er_definitions.php |publisher=University of Wisconsin–Madison |access-date=12 August 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071027103517/http://registrar.wisc.edu/students/acadrecords/enrollment_reports/85_er_definitions.php |archive-date=27 October 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
